lections.title_en: The Death of the Prophet Isaiah
lections.text_en: The prophet Isaiah was the son of Amos, from Tekoa, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord spoke many messages through the prophet Isaiah to the people of Israel. And after these words which the Lord spoke to Isaiah, he was killed by Manasseh, sawn in two, and was laid beneath the oak of Rogel, near the channels of the water which King Hezekiah had destroyed by blocking it. For this reason God worked the signs of Siloam for the sake of the prophet. For before he died he was distressed by thirst, and at once [water] was sent to him. Therefore it was called Siloam, which is translated “sent.”

lections.title_en: The Life of the Prophet Zechariah
lections.text_en: Zechariah was of the tribe of Levi, and was born in Kargdi, in the land of the Chaldeans. He prophesied much about the people, and gave a sign for the confirmation of his words. He said concerning Jozadak that he would beget a son, and that he would serve as priest in Jerusalem in blamelessness, after the pattern of the true High Priest. He also blessed Shealtiel, and said, “You will beget a son, and you shall call his name Zerubbabel.” And to Cyrus he gave a sign of victory; and concerning his service he said beforehand what he was to do in Jerusalem, and he blessed him greatly. And he prophesied about the things to come in Jerusalem: about its end, and the beginning of the nations, and the emptiness of the priests, and of the prophets, and of the sabbaths; and he indicated the double judgment. And he died in peace in a good old age, and was buried near Haggai.

lections.title_en: Jeremiah and the Ark of the Covenant
lections.text_en: The prophet Jeremiah, before the destruction of the temple, took the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and whatever Moses had placed in it. These are: the stone tablet of the law of God, inscribed by God; and the rod of Aaron, which blossomed, with the fruit of the nut; and the golden jar full of manna from heaven; and the bronze censer, which was changed into gold by the hand of Aaron. These were in the ark. The prophet took it, and carried it to Mount Sinai, and placed it there in the rock, and the rock swallowed up the ark; and the prophet sealed the name of God upon the rock; and a bright cloud came and covered the name of God. And no one knew the place, and no one was able to read that writing until this day.

lections.title_en: The Repose of the Blessed John, Apostle, Theologian and Evangelist
lections.text_en: The blessed John was with the brothers in great joy in the Lord. And on a certain Lord’s day all the brothers were gathered to him, and he began to speak with them thus: “My brothers, fellow servants, fellow heirs and partakers of the kingdom of the Lord, you know how great a power God gave you through my hand. How many signs, how many marvels, how many graces; what teachings, oversights, rests, ministries, glories, faiths, unions, endowments, gifts! How much and how many [things] you saw with your own eyes, of what was given to you, which are not seen by these eyes, nor will be heard by these ears. Now be established in him, remembering him in all your works. You know the mystery of the dispensation that came about among men, for whose sake the Lord did it. The Lord himself, through me, entreats you, brothers, and prays that you remain without insults, without deceit, without dissoluteness. For he knows the insults that come from you; he knows also the contempt, he knows also the deceit, and he knows also the dissoluteness, in your turning away from his holy commandments. Now let not God the benefactor be grieved by you: the Compassionate and Merciful, the Holy, the Pure, the Spotless, the Immaterial, the Only One, the Sole One, the Unchangeable, the True, the Guileless, the One without Wrath, who is above every name that can be spoken or thought, my God Jesus. Now, let him rejoice in our good religious life. May he rejoice in our holy life; may he rest in our modest conduct; may he be free of care in our self-restraint; may he be pleased in our unity; may he smile at our sobriety; may he delight in our loving him. These things I say to you now, brothers, as you hasten to your coming works, [you who are] already perfected in the Lord. For what else shall I have to say to you? You have the pledge of your God; you have the gifts of his beneficence; you have his inevitable coming. For if you sin no more, God will forgive you what you did in ignorance; but if, having known him, and having found mercy from him, you still conduct yourselves in the same way, he will also reckon the former sins against you, and you will not receive mercy from him.” And having said this to them, he stood in prayer, thus: “You who wove this crown with your own weaving, Jesus. You who joined these many flowers from your unfading flower. You who sowed these life-giving words of yours. You who alone are the caretaker of your servants, and the physician who heals freely. You who alone are good and without arrogance. You who alone are merciful and the lover of mankind. You who alone are Savior and righteous. You who always are, and in all, and are near everywhere, my God Jesus: cover with your gifts all who hope in you. You who know everywhere the devices and the violence of our slanderer.” And then, having asked for bread, he gave thanks thus: “What blessing, or what offering, or what thanksgiving shall we name in the breaking of this bread, other than you alone, Jesus Christ?”

lections.text_en: And the Lord will come to the land, and will walk about among men. And the oak which is by the torrent shall be divided into twelve oaks. And they shall go after [him], and shall obey the God who appears. And by him shall every man live.
